I’ve been feeling really off for a few months now. I used to be into online gaming and playing pickup basketball, but lately I just can’t make myself care. Even when friends text to hang out, I just ignore it or say I’m tired.

My mind keeps going back to what happened last year. Sometimes it’s like I’m not even in the present anymore. I’ll hear a loud noise, or a car backfire, and suddenly I’m right back there, like it’s actually happening again. My heart just starts pounding and my hands shake, and it takes a long time to calm down, even when I know I’m safe.

I keep replaying it and thinking, “If he hadn’t done that, none of this would’ve happened,” and I get stuck on how it was other people’s fault. The fear I felt then still kind of sits in my chest, like it never really went away.

Day to day stuff feels hard. Even choosing what to wear, or what to eat, I’ll just stare at things, unable to decide. I’m supposed to be applying for jobs, but I put it off and feel kind of empty and stuck.
D018-D013_h001.question_a:
It’s been a little over a year since the car accident, and it still feels like I never left it. I’ll be walking down the street or trying to fill out an online job application, and suddenly I’m back there—metal crunching, glass everywhere, my heart racing. In those moments it’s not like a memory; it’s like it’s happening again. I can smell the smoke, hear the sirens. I just freeze.

Since then, I’ve kind of stopped doing the things I used to like. I don’t play soccer with my friends anymore, don’t really game with them either. I mostly stay in my room. I keep replaying it in my head and getting angry at the other driver and even at my friend who asked me for that ride—I keep thinking if they hadn’t, none of this would’ve happened.

The fear from that night never really went away. Loud noises or sudden braking on a bus make my heart pound and my hands shake for a long time; I can’t calm down. Even basic stuff—picking clothes, choosing what to eat, deciding which jobs to apply for—feels overwhelming. I feel down a lot, but it all circles back to that crash.
D018-D013_h001.question_b:
I’ve been feeling really low for about eight months now, pretty much every day. It started a little after that car accident last year. Since then, it’s like the color’s drained out of everything. Stuff I used to enjoy—playing soccer with friends, gaming, even just watching shows—just doesn’t feel like anything. I mostly stay in my room, sleeping a lot or just lying there, feeling tired and guilty that I’m not doing more with my life.

I do think back to the accident a lot, and sometimes when I hear tires screech or a loud crash, my heart starts racing and my hands shake for a while before I can calm down. Once or twice I’ve kind of “zoned out” and felt like I was back there for a few seconds, but mostly it’s just regular memories, not like I’m reliving it all the time. I know it wasn’t really anyone’s fault, even though sometimes I catch myself being angry at the other driver.

It feels less like I’m stuck in that moment and more like I’ve just never really bounced back mood-wise. I’m constantly down, unmotivated, and it’s making it hard to even apply for jobs or make simple choices, like what to wear or what to eat.

I guess this really started maybe a few months ago… it’s hard to pin down exactly. I still go to work most days, but I’m not really “there.” I’ll be trimming hedges or using the blower and suddenly it’s like I’m back in that moment from last year when the accident happened on site. For a few seconds I forget I’m in someone’s garden. I can smell it, hear it, like it’s happening again. Then I kind of snap out of it and feel shaky and embarrassed.

Since then I’ve been keeping to myself a lot more. The lads from work ask me out for a drink and I always make some excuse. Even with my family, I don’t really answer calls. I just feel like I’m not much fun to be around, and part of me thinks it was my fault anyway, that I should’ve done something differently that day.

I’m on edge all the time. If someone drops a tool or a car backfires, I jump out of my skin. It’s awkward when a client notices. My mind wanders a lot too; I’ll reread the same text or forget what someone just told me. Most evenings I just sit at home feeling tense and low, but I’m not sure if it’s just stress or something else.
D018-D013_h002.question_a:
It started about eight months ago, after that car crash on the highway when the other driver died. Since then it’s like part of me is still stuck there. Sometimes when I’m out on a job and a truck backfires or brakes screech, I’m suddenly right back in the car. I don’t just remember it—I feel the seatbelt, I smell the smoke, I’m bracing for the impact. For a few seconds I forget I’m standing in someone’s garden.

I keep replaying it and thinking I should’ve reacted faster, taken a different route, something. I can’t shake the feeling that it’s my fault. I used to go out with my mates after work, but now I mostly make excuses and stay home. I don’t really feel like talking to anyone.

I’m tense all the time, jumpy. If someone drops a tool or there’s a loud bang I flinch hard, my heart races. My boss has noticed I lose track of what I’m doing—watering the same bed twice, zoning out mid-conversation. I do feel low a lot, but it all seems wrapped up in what happened in that crash.
D018-D013_h002.question_b:
It all really started after that accident on site about eight months ago, when a retaining wall collapsed and nearly crushed my coworker. I still get these moments, especially when I’m working near stone or hear machinery, where it’s like I’m briefly back there watching it fall. It only lasts a few seconds, and I know where I am, but it’s like a vivid replay in my head.

I keep thinking I should’ve noticed the cracks sooner, that it’s my fault for not speaking up. I’ve pulled back from the lads at work and my mates; I don’t go to the pub with them anymore and mostly just go straight home. I feel on edge a lot of the time, kind of tense and worried, but it’s not like I’m constantly reliving it or avoiding everything to do with the job.

I’m more just…down. No energy, nothing feels enjoyable, I struggle to get out of bed even on days off. I can’t focus when the foreman’s talking through plans, my mind drifts. If a shovel drops or a truck backfires, I jump more than I used to, which is embarrassing. Overall it’s this heavy, low mood that’s there most days, more than anything else.

Since my husband died and that whole mess around his last days, I keep getting these pictures in my head, like little films that start playing without my permission. I’ll be sitting in my chair and suddenly I’m right back there, hearing the machines, seeing his face. It just pops in, even when I’m trying to read or watch my shows, and then I lose track of what I was doing.

I don’t seem to enjoy much anymore. The garden’s gone to weeds; I used to fuss over every rose, but now I just look at it and feel… nothing, really. When the grandchildren visit, I try to be happy, but it feels like I’m watching myself pretend.

I keep thinking the doctors should’ve done more, or my son should’ve pushed harder, and I get stuck on that. The fear from that time hasn’t really left; it’s like it’s sitting just under my skin. D018-D013_h003.question_a:
It’s been about a year now since my husband died in that car accident, but it feels like it’s still happening. I keep getting these pictures in my head, almost like little films I can’t turn off—him trapped in the car, the phone call from the police. They just pop in when I’m making tea or trying to read, and I’m right back there. The fear I felt that night hasn’t really gone away; it still feels like a terrible shock sitting in my chest.

Since then, it’s like the light went out. I don’t really feel joy anymore—not with my grandkids, not with my garden, not with the church group I used to enjoy. I mostly feel numb and sad. I catch myself thinking, “If the paramedics had gotten there sooner,” or “If my daughter hadn’t asked him to drive that night,” none of this would’ve happened. I know it’s not fair, but I can’t stop assigning blame.

I jump at every loud sound now—if a door slams or a car backfires, I physically flinch. Even following a TV show or a simple conversation is hard; my mind just drifts back to the accident. All this sadness and emptiness feels tied to what happened that night, not like the low moods I had before.
D018-D013_h003.question_b:
It really started after my husband passed away about a year and a half ago. I’ve been low before, but this feels different, like the light went out. I don’t really enjoy anything anymore—my garden, church, even seeing the great‑grandkids on video calls. I feel flat, like I’m just going through the motions.

I think about the day he died, of course, but it’s more like a sad memory than something that keeps ambushing me. I don’t get those vivid re-experiencing episodes people describe. I’m mostly just exhausted and empty, and I wake up wondering what the point is. I feel guilty, like I should have noticed his health getting worse sooner, but I also know in my head it wasn’t really anyone’s fault.

I have trouble concentrating on my books or even following a TV show, my mind just drifts. Loud noises don’t make me jump out of my skin; I’m more likely not to notice them. I’m not reliving horror—I’m just stuck in this gray fog of sadness that never really lifts.
